cases.reason: SR7a defers to the relation-condition rules, and those differ in a way that makes some EVALUATE operands NARROWER in 2002. 2002 general-relation SR2 leaves class index out of the classes an identifier may have; 2023 SR2 adds it. Read that way, 2002 requires a diagnostic for EVALUATE IXD1 WHEN IXD2 (two USAGE INDEX data items), which 2023 permits. But 2002's own 8.8.4.1.1 list item 8 and 8.8.4.1.1.10 item 3 allow comparing an index data item with another index data item, so the 2002 text contradicts itself. Probe: the compiler accepts the program at both editions and prints EQUAL. The 2023 row's evidence (pb399, pb47, pb398) never uses an index data item. What would settle it: a signed 2002 derivation that chooses between 8.8.4.1.1.2 SR2 and 8.8.4.1.1.10 for an index data item used as identifier-1/identifier-2 of a general relation (and so as an EVALUATE operand). If SR2 governs, the compiler is wrong at 2002. The renumbered reference (8.8.4.1.1 -> 8.8.4.2) is otherwise a superset.

cases.reason: The rule defers through STOP to normal run unit termination, and that clause has a communication-facility rule in 2002 that 2023 lacks. In 2002, a GOBACK executed in a program not under a calling runtime element 'operates as if executing a STOP statement'. 2002 STOP GR1 performs 14.5.10, whose rule 2 purges partially received messages and SEND portions not ended by an EMI or EGI from the MCS. 2002 Annex A lists 14.5.10 rule 2 as a communications-facility entity. 2023's chain (GOBACK GR3 -> STOP GR1 -> 14.6.11) has no such rule. So the 2002 rule covers a main program that used the communication facility and ends with GOBACK, and no 2023 row can show that case. The compiler implements the facility at --std 2002: probe goback_main_mcs compiles with the COBOL0903 obsolete warning, SENDs a 5-character text with no EMI/EGI indicator and ends with GOBACK. At 2023 the same program is refused (COBOL0902). Whether the partial message is purged at termination cannot be seen from the program.

cases.reason: SR3 defers to MOVE validity, and the MOVE rules changed. 2002 MOVE SR5 forbids only SPACE to a numeric or numeric-edited item. 2023 MOVE SR5 forbids every alphanumeric figurative constant (QUOTE, HIGH-VALUE, LOW-VALUE, non-digit ALL), keeping only ALL digits to an integer item. In 2002 a figurative constant may stand wherever 'literal' appears (8.3.1.2.5.2 SR1), so literal-1 may be HIGH-VALUE. INITIALIZE G REPLACING NUMERIC DATA BY HIGH-VALUE (or BY QUOTE) is therefore valid under 2002 SR3 and invalid under 2023 SR4. The 2023 row records a refusal of exactly that program, which says nothing about the 2002 acceptance this rule requires. Probe: at --std 2002 the compiler accepts it and runs (A=, DONE). At 2023 it is refused with COBOL0902 citing §2023:14.9.20.3 SR4. The compiler is correct at 2002.
